concepts.book: Going Deeper with New Testament Greek

world.name: One street, eleven stops
world.line: Bathe, shout, fence, drive, sail, point, paint, answer, record, forecast, chime.
world.why: Eleven places on one street, walked in the order the book teaches them. You are not remembering a list of cases; you are remembering where you are standing. Every new chapter opens another door on the same street.

words.mn: ah-pahng-GHEHL-lo ≈ "a PANG — hard-G HELLO!" A pang, then you hail everyone: ANNOUNCE.
ah-po-THEE-tho-mee ≈ "a-PO-THEE-tho-me." ἀπό back + δίδωμι give — hand it back over: I PAY, I RETURN.
AH-rah ≈ "AH — RAH!" The cheer once the point lands: SO, THEN.
ah-FEH-sees ≈ "a-FESS-sis." Fess up, sis — and it is FORGIVEN.
AH-khree ≈ "a CRY" (rasped: kh). You cry UNTIL it is over.
VAHP-tees-mah ≈ "VOP-TEASE-ma." Spelled βαπτ-, our BAPTISM — Koine β says "v".
THEV-teh-ros ≈ "THE-VET-ROSE." Spelled δευτ-, our DEUTERONOMY: the SECOND law.
thee-ah-ko-NEH-o ≈ "THEE-a-ko-NAY-o." Spelled διακον-, our DEACON, who waits the tables: I SERVE.
thee-EHR-kho-meh ≈ "THE-AIR-I-COMB." You comb right THROUGH the air.
ehk-po-REV-o-meh ≈ "ECK-po-REV-o-me." Rev it up and GO OUT.

words.gloss: I clothe myself, put on, wear
words.mn: ehn-THEW-o ≈ "en-THEW-oh." A DUO of sleeves goes on at once — our own en-DUE: I PUT ON, I WEAR.
eh-pee-ghee-NOS-ko ≈ "a-PIGGY-KNOWS-ko." A piggy KNOWS you: RECOGNIZE.
EH-ray-mos ≈ "AIR-RAY-MOSS." Air and rays, no moss at all: the DESERT.
heh-TEW-mah-zo ≈ "he-and-YOU-ma-zo." He and YOU get it all READY together.
EH-tos ≈ "a TOSS." You toss the old calendar out each YEAR.
ev-tho-KEH-o ≈ "EV-tho-KAY-o." εὖ well + δοκέω seem: it seems good to him — WELL PLEASED.
ay-sah-EE-ahs ≈ "a-SAY-EE-as." Say it and you have ISAIAH.
THAY-ree-on ≈ "THEY'RE-ON." They're on me — the wild BEASTS!
THLEEP-sees ≈ "the-LIPS-SEIZE." The lips seize under the pressure: TRIBULATION.
THREEX ≈ "THREE-X." Three strands of HAIR crossed in an X.
hee-kah-NOS ≈ "HE-CAN-nose." He can do it — he is ABLE.
ee-or-THAH-nays ≈ "YOUR-THAW-nays." Spelled Ἰορδ-, the JORDAN, its δ sounding "th".
ees-KHEW-ros ≈ "EES-KHEW-ros" (rasped: kh). ἰσχύς is muscle — he muscles through: STRONG, mighty.

words.gloss: I cause to sit down, appoint
words.mn: kah-THEE-zo ≈ "KATHY-EATS-oh." Kathy eats, so Kathy SITS DOWN.
krah-TEH-o ≈ "ka-RA-TE-o." KARATE is all grip and hold: I GRASP, HOLD FAST, ARREST.
meh-tah-NEW-ah ≈ "ME? a-NEW-ah!" Me, made new — a changed mind: REPENTANCE.
nah-OS ≈ "NOAH'S." Noah's holy house: the TEMPLE.
ho-MEW-os ≈ "ho-MEW-os." The ὁμο- of HOMOgeneous — all of one kind: LIKE, similar.
o-PEE-so ≈ "OH-PEE-so." Opie tags along AFTER you, always BEHIND.
oo-EH ≈ "oo-AY!" Said aloud it is already a wail: WOE!
oo-KEH-tee ≈ "ooh-KETTLE." The kettle is NO LONGER boiling.
pee-RAH-zo ≈ "PEER-RAH-zo." He peers at you to TEST you.
po-tah-MOS ≈ "a-POT-o'-MOSS." It floats away down the RIVER.

words.gloss: before, in front of, at (+ gen.)
words.mn: PRO ≈ "a PRO." The pro always goes BEFORE the rookie.
pros-FEH-ro ≈ "PROS-FERRY-o." The pros ferry it over and OFFER it.
sah-tah-NAHS ≈ "SATAN-ahs." The accuser himself: SATAN.
STAV-ro-o ≈ "STOW-a-ROW-oh." They STOW him away on a row of timber: they CRUCIFY him.
tehs-seh-rah-KON-tah ≈ "TESS-and-SARAH-COUNT-ah." They count to FORTY.
few-lah-KAY ≈ "a-FEW-lo-KAY." A few locked away, Kay: PRISON, a GUARD.
KHO-rah ≈ "CORA" (rasped: kh). Cora owns the whole REGION.
AH-ghree-os ≈ "ANGRY-os." Angry and untamed: WILD.
ah-KREES ≈ "a-CREASE." The locusts eat a crease across the field: LOCUST.
vo-AH-o ≈ "a VOW — AH — OH!" Every syllable of it is a shout: he CRIES OUT.
thehr-mah-TEE-nos ≈ "THERMAL-TEE-nos." Spelled δερμ-, our DERMATOLOGY — skin, so (made of) LEATHER.
ehx-o-mo-lo-GHEH-o ≈ "EGGS-o-mo-lo-GAY-o." He logs it all out loud: CONFESS.
ev-THEWS ≈ "EV — THOSE!" Ev sends those STRAIGHT ahead.
ZO-nay ≈ "a ZONE-ay." The BELT is the zone around your waist.
hee-eh-ro-so-lew-MEE-tays ≈ "HIERO-SO-LEW-mee-tays." A JERUSALEM-ite.
hee-MAHS ≈ "HE-MASHED." He mashed the sandal STRAP flat.
kah-MAY-los ≈ "ka-MAY-los." Say it and it is already the CAMEL.
kah-tah-SKEV-ah-zo ≈ "CUT-a-SKEV-a-zo." Cut it, skewer it, PREPARE the feast.
KEWP-to ≈ "CUTE-P-toe" — like "cute" with a P. He stoops low: BEND DOWN.
MEH-lee ≈ "MEL-ee." Mel loves his HONEY.
nah-zah-REHT ≈ "NAZA-RET." The town itself: NAZARETH.
os-FEWS ≈ "OS-FEWS." The few bones at your WAIST.
peh-ree-steh-RAH ≈ "PERRY'S-STAIR-ah." A DOVE settles on Perry's stair.

words.gloss: I split, divide, separate, tear apart
words.mn: SKHEE-zo ≈ "SKIS-oh." The skis SPLIT the snow apart.
TREE-vos ≈ "TREE-VOSS." The PATH worn between the trees.
hew-po-THAY-mah ≈ "WHO-put-THEM-ah?" The SANDALS, of course.
ah-GHROS ≈ "a GROSS." A gross of wheat standing in the FIELD.
ah-kah-THAHR-tos ≈ "a-CATHARTIC-os." A cathartic cleanses — and the ἀ- cancels it: UNCLEAN.
ah-kro-VEW-stee-ah ≈ "ACRO-VEW-stee-ah." An ACROBAT keeps his ἄκρον, his tip, exactly as it was: UNCIRCUMCISION.
ah-nah-ghee-NOS-ko ≈ "ANNA-GHEE-KNOWS-ko." Anna knows her letters — she READS it aloud.
AH-neh-mos ≈ "AH-neh-MOSS." It lifts the moss right off the stone — an ANEMOmeter measures it: the WIND.
ahr-NEH-o-meh ≈ "ARE? NAY! — o-me." Asked, and he says nay: I DENY it.
veev-LEE-on ≈ "VEEV-lee-on." Our word BIBLE, softened: the BOOK, the scroll.

words.gloss: covenant, decree, last will and testament
words.mn: thee-ah-THAY-kay ≈ "THEE-a-THAY-kay." διά between + τίθημι place — terms laid down between two parties: a COVENANT, a last will.
thee-ah-ko-NEE-ah ≈ "THEE-a-CONE-ee-ah." The root of DEACON, its δ softened to "th": MINISTRY.
thee-KEH-o-o ≈ "THEE? OKAY-o!" Thee — okay, you are in the right. From δίκαιος: I JUSTIFY, I VINDICATE.
thee-O-tee ≈ "THEE-O-tee" — you can hear THEO in it, God. Why did any of it happen? BECAUSE of him. For, because, therefore.
thew-nah-TOS ≈ "THEW-not-a-TOSS." Do NOT toss this one aside — spelled δυν-, our DYNAMITE: POWERFUL, able.
ehng-GHEWS ≈ "en-GOOSE." The goose is right there at your heel — NEAR, close to.
ehx-eh-STEEN ≈ "EX-EH-STEEN" — all but EXISTING. It is lawful for this to exist: IT IS PERMITTED.
eh-pee-ghno-SEES ≈ "a-PIGGY-KNOWS-ees." What the piggy knows in full: KNOWLEDGE.
ev-THEH-os ≈ "EV-THEH-os." εὐ- well + θέω run: run straight there and arrive IMMEDIATELY.
ehkh-THROS ≈ "EXTRA-GROSS." Extra gross to you: HOSTILE, hated.
HAY-lee-os ≈ "HELIOS / HELIUM." Helium was found in the SUN.
hee-eh-REVS ≈ "HE-EVER-REVS." He ever revs the altar coals — ἱερός is holy: the PRIEST.
kah-thah-REE-zo ≈ "CATHARSIS-o." Catharsis is a washing out: I CLEANSE.
kah-tahr-GHEH-o ≈ "ka-TAR-GHEH-o." A KARATE chop to it — κατά down + ἀργός idle: I CANCEL, MAKE VOID.
lo-GHEE-zo-meh ≈ "lo-GEE-zo-may." Same root as LOGIC and LOGarithm — you tot it up: I RECKON, I ACCOUNT.
MEH-los ≈ "ME-LOSS." Me, and the loss of a limb: a MEMBER, a part of the body.
NEH ≈ "NEH." Careful — it sounds like our "nay" but means the opposite: YES.
new-NEE ≈ "NEW-nee." What is new is what is NOW.
or-GHAY ≈ "ORGY." An ORGY is what calls down the WRATH: ANGER, and the punishment after it.
OOS ≈ "OOZE." Cup it and listen — the EAR.
pah-rah-ghee-NO-meh ≈ "PARA-GHEE-no-may." The PARAchute drops him in right beside you: I ARRIVE, I APPEAR.
pahr-ray-SEE-ah ≈ "PARTY-SIRI-ah." Ask Siri at the party — she answers anyone, out loud, no hesitation: BOLDNESS.
peh-ree-to-MAY ≈ "PERI-TOMY." Peri- is around, -tomy is a cut: CIRCUMCISION.
PLAYN ≈ "PLAY ON." Play on — YET, however, the score has changed.
PEW-os ≈ "PYEH-os" — close to Russian поезд, a train. WHAT KIND of train is this?
po-TAY-ree-on ≈ "POTTERY-on." Pottery is what the CUP is made of.
POO ≈ "POO." WHERE did that come from?
pto-KHOS ≈ "p-TOE-KHOS" (rasped: kh). Poor OJOS — eyes hollow from hunger: POOR, a beggar.
hew-po-STREH-fo ≈ "HUE-po-STROPHE-o." A strophe is a turn — turn back: RETURN.
hew-steh-REH-o ≈ "HYSTER-eh-o." Hysteros is later — he came in last: I FALL SHORT.
fah-neh-RO-o ≈ "fa-NAR-o-o" — Russian фонарь, a flashlight. Shine it and the thing is seen: I REVEAL.
FEE-leep-pos ≈ "PHILIP with an F." Philip.
kho-REES ≈ "WHO-REES." Who are you WITHOUT him? Apart from, without.

words.gloss: freely, as a gift, without payment
it happens before, be done before
I present, put forward, display publicly

words.mn: ah-gho-RAH-zo ≈ "the AGORA-zo." The ἀγορά is the marketplace — where you go to BUY.
ah-thee-KEH-o ≈ "ah-THEE-KAY-o." Ah, thee? Okay — and he hands you the short end of a rigged scale. ἀ- strips out the δίκη, the justice: I TREAT UNJUSTLY.
ah-lay-thee-NOS ≈ "a-LAY-THEE-NOSE." Lay thee nose against it — no crack, no fake: GENUINE.
ah-NAHNG-kay ≈ "a-NAG — KAY!" A nag, Kay, that will not let up: NECESSITY, pressure.
HAH-pahx ≈ "HA! — PACKS." He packs it away once, and never again: ONCE FOR ALL.
ahr-NEE-on ≈ "ARE-KNEE-on." Down on your knees before the LAMB.
hahr-PAH-zo ≈ "HARP-AH-zo." A harpy, and our HARPOON: it SNATCHES its prey.
vahr-nah-VAHS ≈ "VAR-na-VAHS." Both β's say "v" in Koine: BARNABAS.
ghah-MEH-o ≈ "GAM-MAY-o." Gam — May! He asks for her hand in May: I MARRY. (Our monoGAMY.)
GHNO-sees ≈ "g-NO-SEES." An aGNOStic is one without it: KNOWLEDGE.
thee-ah-KREE-no ≈ "DEE-a-CREE-no" — spelled with δ, so it is said "th". To DIscriminate is to sort two things apart: I JUDGE between — or waver and DOUBT.
eh-leh-EH-o ≈ "EL-eh-EH-o." Kyrie ELEISON — Lord, HAVE MERCY.
EH-leh-os ≈ "ELL-eh-oss." The noun standing behind eleison: MERCY itself.
eh-pee-thew-MEE-ah ≈ "a-PEA-THEW-ME-ah." ἐπί upon + θυμός passion — the heart set on it: CRAVING.
eh-pee-kah-LEH-o ≈ "EPIC-a-LAY-o." An EPIC call, shouted over everyone’s head: I CALL UPON, I NAME.
eh-pee-tee-MAH-o ≈ "a-PEE-TEE-MOW." He mows you down with a word: I REBUKE, reprove, WARN.
hay-gheh-O-meh ≈ "HAY-GO-may." Hay, go! — he is already out in front: I LEAD, and so I RECKON it best.
thew-GHAH-tayr ≈ "THEW-GATOR." Daddy’s little GATOR, all teeth and trouble: the DAUGHTER.
thew-SEE-ah ≈ "THEW-SEE-ya." One last see-ya as it goes up in smoke: the SACRIFICE, the offering.
ee-ah-KO-vos ≈ "ee-a-CO-VOS." Jacob in Greek dress — which English turned into JAMES.
EE-theh ≈ "EE-THE." One syllable and a pointing finger: LOOK!
ee-OO-thahs ≈ "ee-OO-THAHS." One name for all three: JUDAS, Jude, Judah.
KEH-sahr ≈ "KAY-SAR." Not "see-zer" — Koine αι is "eh": CAESAR.
mah-KHEH-rah ≈ "ma-KHEH-rah" (rasped: kh). Russian махать, to wave — she waves the blade: the SWORD.
meem-NAY-sko-meh ≈ "meem-NAY-sko-may." The root of MNEMONIC itself — the whole point of these hooks: I REMEMBER.
mee-SEH-o ≈ "ME-SAY-o." A MISanthrope says it of everyone: I HATE.
mees-THOS ≈ "MISS-THOSE." Miss those and you worked all day for nothing: PAY, WAGES, reward.
pah-rah-KLAY-sees ≈ "PARA-CLAY-sees." The PARACLETE is called alongside you: COMFORT.
pah-REHR-kho-meh ≈ "pa-RARE-ko-may" (rasped: kh). παρά alongside + ἔρχομαι come: I PASS BY.
PAHS-khah ≈ "PAS-KHA." Pascha itself, barely changed: the PASSOVER.
po-TEH ≈ "po-TAY." "Once upon a po-TAY" — ONCE, formerly, ever.
skahn-thah-LEE-zo ≈ "SCAN-THAL-ee-zo." Spelled σκανδαλ-, our SCANDAL — Koine δ says "th": I MAKE THEM STUMBLE.
SKO-tos ≈ "SCO-TOSS." Toss the lamp out and this is what is left: DARKNESS.
sew-nee-THAY-sees ≈ "SEW-knee-THEY-sees." σύν with + οἶδα know — knowing along with yourself: CONSCIENCE.
so-TAYR ≈ "so-TARE." SOTERiology is the doctrine of him: the SAVIOR.
so-tay-REE-ah ≈ "so-tay-REE-ah." What the σωτήρ brings with him: SALVATION.
FEE-los ≈ "FEEL-oss." PHILadelphia is love of the brother: a FRIEND, beloved.
FO-vos ≈ "FOE-VOSS." Our PHOBIA — but here it can also mean reverence: FEAR.
few-LAHS-so ≈ "a-FEW-LASSO." A few lassos thrown round the flock: I GUARD.
few-LAY ≈ "a-FEW-LAY." A few lay claim to one bloodline: a TRIBE.
ah-thee-KEE-ah ≈ "a-THEE-KEY-ah." ἀ- not + δίκη justice, Koine δ as "th": INJUSTICE.
ah-lay-THAYS ≈ "a-LAY-THAYS." Lay it out and nothing is hidden: TRUE, honest.

words.gloss: I look up, see again, receive sight
words.mn: ah-nah-VLEH-po ≈ "ANNA-VLEP-o." ἀνά up + βλέπω see: I LOOK UP — and the blind SEE AGAIN.
AHR-tee ≈ "ARTY." The arty crowd care about nothing but NOW.
ahs-theh-NAYS ≈ "as-THEN-AYS." Our ASTHENIA, without strength: WEAK, sick.
vahs-TAH-zo ≈ "VAS-TAH-zo." Spelled βαστ- but Koine β says "v": he hoists the vase and BEARS it.
GHAH-mos ≈ "GAM-oss." MonoGAMy is one of these: a MARRIAGE.
GHEH ≈ "GEH" (hard g). One breath of emphasis and no more: INDEED.
GHEV-o-meh ≈ "GAV-o-may." Gav gave me a spoonful to TASTE.
ghno-REE-zo ≈ "g-NO-REE-zo." Built on γνῶσις, knowledge: I MAKE IT KNOWN.
THEH-kah ≈ "THECK-ah." Our DECAthlon and DECAde — Koine δ says "th": TEN.
THEHN-thron ≈ "THEN-THRON." A rhoDODENDRon is a rose-TREE.
thee-AH-ko-nos ≈ "THEE-A-ko-nos." Spelled δια-, our DEACON: a SERVANT.

words.gloss: I am a slave, serve, obey
words.mn: thoo-LEV-o ≈ "THOO-LEV-o." A δοῦλος is a slave, and this is his life: I SERVE.
ehk-KHEH-o ≈ "eck-KAY-o" (rasped: kh). ἐκ out + χέω pour: I POUR IT OUT.
HEHL-layn ≈ "HELL-ayn." HELLENistic is named for him: a GREEK.

words.gloss: because of, on account of, for the sake of
words.mn: HEH-neh-kah ≈ "HEN-eh-ka." All this fuss on account of one hen: BECAUSE OF.
HAY-ko ≈ "HAY-ko." Hay-ho — I HAVE COME.
ee-ah-KOV ≈ "ee-a-COV." The Hebrew form left undressed: JACOB.
kah-thah-ROS ≈ "ka-THA-ROSE." A CATHARtic leaves you CLEAN, pure.
KEE-meh ≈ "KEY-may." The key may just LIE there where it fell.
lew-PEH-o ≈ "LOO-PAY-o." Loo, pay up — and it GRIEVES you.
mah-REE-ah ≈ "ma-REE-ah." The Greek spelling: MARY.
mah-ree-AHM ≈ "ma-ree-AHM." The Hebrew spelling of the same name: MARY.
mews-TAY-ree-on ≈ "MUSE-TAY-ree-on." Straight across into English: MYSTERY.
nee-KAH-o ≈ "NIKE-ah-o." NIKE is victory herself: I CONQUER.
newm-FEE-os ≈ "NUMF-EE-os." The NYMPH is the bride; this is her man: the BRIDEGROOM.
EW-nos ≈ "EW-nos." Koine οι says "ew"; our OENOlogy is the study of WINE.
pnev-mah-tee-KOS ≈ "p-NEV-ma-TEE-kos." πνεῦμα is breath and spirit — PNEUMAtic: SPIRITUAL.
PO-thehn ≈ "PO-THEN." Po — then where did it come from? FROM WHERE?
PO-sos ≈ "PO-SOS." An SOS always asks HOW MUCH is left.
pro-fay-TEV-o ≈ "pro-fay-TEV-o." Say it aloud and it is already the word: I PROPHESY.
SOS ≈ "SOSS." Short, blunt and possessive: YOUR.
stav-ROS ≈ "STAV-ROSE." The noun behind σταυρόω, and a stave of wood: the CROSS.
strah-tee-O-tays ≈ "STRAT-ee-O-tays." STRATegy is his trade: a SOLDIER.
sew-NEE-ay-mee ≈ "SEW-KNEE-ay-me." σύν together + ἵημι send: you put it together and UNDERSTAND.
teh-LEH-o ≈ "TELL-AY-o." τέλος is the end — tell them it is FINISHED.
fro-NEH-o ≈ "FRO-NAY-o." SchizoPHRENia splits this very thing: the mind — I THINK.
fo-NEH-o ≈ "FONE-AY-o." A phone exists for exactly this: I CALL.
KHAY-rah ≈ "KAY-rah" (rasped: kh). Kay, left on her own now: the WIDOW.
hah-mahr-to-LOS ≈ "ha-MAR-to-LOSS." He marred it, and it is his loss — ἁμαρτία is missing the mark: a SINNER.
ahm-peh-LON ≈ "AMPLE-LAWN." An ample lawn of vines: the VINEYARD.
ah-NAH-gho ≈ "a-NA-go." ἀνά up + ἄγω lead: I LEAD UP, I bring back — and at sea, I set sail.
ah-neh-REH-o ≈ "a-NAIR-AY-o." ἀνά up + αἱρέω take — he takes it up and away for good: I DESTROY, I KILL.
AH-pees-tos ≈ "AH-PEACE-toss." Peace tossed out — ἀ- not + πίστις faith: FAITHLESS, unbelieving.
ahs-THEH-nee-ah ≈ "as-THEN-ee-ah." Our ASTHENIA: WEAKNESS, sickness.

words.gloss: I am weak, sick, in need
words.mn: ahs-theh-NEH-o ≈ "as-THEN-AY-o." The verb of the same root: I AM WEAK, sick, in need.
ahs-TAYR ≈ "a-STARE." You stare up at it — and it is our ASTERisk: a STAR.
av-XAH-no ≈ "av-ZA-no." Our AUGment and AUXiliary, both added on: I GROW, INCREASE.
theh-AY-sees ≈ "the-A-sees." The one who sees the need is asked: a PETITION, an entreaty.
ee-KON ≈ "ee-CON." An ICON is exactly this: an IMAGE, a likeness.
eh-LEV-theh-ros ≈ "a-LEV-thuh-ros." No chain on him at all: FREE.
eh-nehr-GHEH-o ≈ "en-ER-GAY-o." Our ENERGY, put to use: I WORK, I PRODUCE.
heh-or-TAY ≈ "he-or-TAY." Hey, or tay — everyone is out dancing: the FESTIVAL.
eh-pees-to-LAY ≈ "a-PIS-to-LAY." Our EPISTLE, laid in your hand: a LETTER.
eh-pees-TREH-fo ≈ "a-PIECE-TREF-o." ἐπί upon + στρέφω turn: I TURN AROUND, I RETURN.
ay-LEE-ahs ≈ "ay-LEE-as." Say it and the prophet is already there: ELIJAH.
ee-AH-o-meh ≈ "ee-AH-o-may." Our PSYCHIATRy and PEDIATRics hold this root: I HEAL, I CURE.
ees-KHEW-o ≈ "EES-KHEW-o" (rasped: kh). The verb beside ἰσχυρός: I AM STRONG, I am able.
kah-tah-LEE-po ≈ "ka-ta-LEAP-o." He leaps away and it stays where it fell: I LEAVE BEHIND, abandon.
keh-LEV-o ≈ "ke-LEV-o." He levels an order at you: I COMMAND, I ORDER.
KREE-sees ≈ "CRISIS." A CRISIS is the moment of decision — and here the verdict: JUDGMENT.
lev-KOS ≈ "LEV-KOSS." LEUKemia is named for the white cells: WHITE, shining.
mahn-THAH-no ≈ "man-THA-no." A MATHematician was first simply a learner: I LEARN.
MAYN ≈ "MAIN." The main measure of a MONTH is the new moon.
MAY-po-teh ≈ "MAY-po-tay." May it not, ever — NEVER; LEST it happen.
MAY-teh ≈ "MAY-tay." May-tay, nor this either: AND NOT, NOR.
neh-FEH-lay ≈ "ne-FELL-ay." NEBULous, and the rain fell from it: a CLOUD.
NOOS ≈ "NOOSE." A noose around your thinking — and the νοῦς is the MIND itself.
om-NEW-o ≈ "om-NEW-o." He starts over with a new vow: I SWEAR, I take an OATH.
PEHS ≈ "PACE." PEDiatrics and PEDagogue are both built on him: the CHILD, the servant.
PAH-ree-mee ≈ "PA-ree-me." παρά beside + εἰμί I am: I AM PRESENT, I have come.
pah-roo-SEE-ah ≈ "pa-roo-SEE-ah." The PAROUSIA itself — his ARRIVAL, his coming.
PEEM-play-mee ≈ "PIMP-LAY-me." Fill it to the brim and lay it down: I FILL, I FULFILL.
PLAY-thos ≈ "PLAY-thoss." PLETHOra is our word for it: a MULTITUDE, a crowd.
por-NEE-ah ≈ "por-NEE-ah." PORNography is named from it: sexual IMMORALITY.
pro-sev-KHAY ≈ "pro-sev-KHAY" (rasped: kh). πρός toward + εὐχή vow — turned toward God: PRAYER.

words.gloss: I pay attention to, devote myself to
words.mn: pro-SEH-kho ≈ "pro-SEK-o" (rasped: kh). πρός toward + ἔχω hold — hold your mind toward it: I PAY ATTENTION.
pros-kah-LEH-o ≈ "pros-ka-LAY-o." πρός toward + καλέω call: I CALL YOU OVER, I SUMMON.
tee-MO-theh-os ≈ "tee-MO-the-os." τιμή honour + θεός God — one who honours God: TIMOTHY.

words.gloss: with the same nature, like in every way

sentences.g: Ἰωάννης ἀπαγγέλλει βάπτισμα μετανοίας εἰς ἄφεσιν.
sentences.e: John announces a baptism of repentance for forgiveness.

sentences.g: ἐκπορεύεται ὁ ὄχλος εἰς τὴν ἔρημον πρὸς τὸν Ἰορδάνην ποταμόν.

sentences.e: He wears camel's hair; but a strong one comes after him.

sentences.g: τεσσεράκοντα ἡμέρας ὁ Σατανᾶς πειράζει αὐτὸν μετὰ τῶν θηρίων.
sentences.e: For forty days Satan tempts him, among the wild animals.

sentences.g: πρὸ τοῦ προσώπου σου ἑτοιμάζω τὴν ὁδόν· διέρχεται γὰρ ὅλην τὴν χώραν.
sentences.e: Before your face I prepare the way, for he goes through the whole region.

sentences.e: They seize him and lead him to prison; the affliction is great, and he speaks no longer.

sentences.e: Woe — they crucify him. So then God repays each one.

sentences.g: οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανός, ἀλλὰ διακονῶ καὶ προσφέρω δῶρα, καὶ ἐπιγινώσκω αὐτόν.
sentences.e: I am not qualified, but I serve and bring gifts, and I recognize him.

sentences.g: ἄχρι τοῦ δευτέρου ἔτους ὅμοιος ἦν τῷ πατρί.
sentences.e: Until the second year he was like his father.

sentences.g: ἀναγινώσκει τὸ βιβλίον τῆς διαθήκης εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας.
sentences.e: He reads the book of the covenant, for knowledge of truth.

sentences.g: εὐθέως ὁ ἥλιος ἀνατέλλει καὶ ὁ ἄνεμος πνεῖ ἐπὶ τὸν ἀγρόν.
sentences.e: Immediately the sun rises and the wind blows over the field.

sentences.g: ὁ ἱερεὺς καθαρίζει τὸ ἀκάθαρτον ποτήριον.
sentences.e: The priest cleanses the unclean cup.

sentences.g: χωρὶς περιτομῆς, ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ, δικαιοῖ ὁ θεός.
sentences.e: Apart from circumcision, in uncircumcision, God justifies.

sentences.g: ναί, νυνὶ λογίζομαι ταῦτα μετὰ παρρησίας.
sentences.e: Yes, now I reckon these things with boldness.

sentences.g: ὁ πτωχὸς ὑστερεῖ· ἔξεστιν οὖν διακονίαν ποιεῖν αὐτῷ.
sentences.e: The poor man lacks; so it is lawful to do him service.

sentences.g: ὁ δυνατὸς καταργεῖ τὸν ἐχθρὸν καὶ τὴν ὀργήν.
sentences.e: The mighty one nullifies the enemy and the wrath.

sentences.g: Φίλιππος παραγίνεται ἐγγὺς καὶ ὑποστρέφει.
sentences.e: Philip arrives nearby and turns back.

sentences.g: τὸ οὖς μέλος ἐστίν· οὐκ ἀρνοῦμαι ὃ ὁ θεὸς φανεροῖ.
sentences.e: The ear is a member; I do not deny what God reveals.

sentences.g: ποῦ καὶ ποίῳ τρόπῳ; πλὴν πιστεύω, διότι ὁ θεὸς λέγει.
sentences.e: Where, and in what kind of way? Yet I believe, because God speaks.

sentences.g: ἀγοράζει ἀρνίον εἰς θυσίαν τοῦ πάσχα.
sentences.e: He buys a lamb for the Passover sacrifice.

sentences.g: ἅπαξ ἐπικαλοῦμαι τὸν σωτῆρα, καὶ ἔχω σωτηρίαν.
sentences.e: Once and for all I call upon the savior, and I have salvation.

sentences.g: ἐλεεῖ ἡμᾶς· τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ παράκλησις τῇ συνειδήσει.
sentences.e: He has mercy on us; his mercy is comfort to the conscience.

sentences.g: Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰούδας καὶ Βαρναβᾶς φίλοι εἰσίν.
sentences.e: James and Jude and Barnabas are friends.

sentences.g: ὁ τοῦ Καίσαρος δοῦλος μαχαίρᾳ φυλάσσει, καὶ φόβος ἐστίν.
sentences.e: Caesar's servant guards with a sword, and there is fear.

sentences.g: μισεῖ καὶ ἀδικεῖ καὶ σκανδαλίζει· διὸ ἐπιτιμῶ αὐτῷ.
sentences.e: He hates and does wrong and causes stumbling; so I rebuke him.

sentences.g: γαμεῖ τὴν θυγατέρα ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς καὶ δίδωσιν μισθόν.
sentences.e: He marries the daughter from the tribe and gives a payment.

sentences.g: ἡ ἐπιθυμία ἐν τῷ σκότει ἁρπάζει· ἀνάγκη ἐστὶν φυγεῖν.
sentences.e: Desire snatches in the darkness; there is a necessity to flee.

sentences.g: ἡγοῦμαι τὴν γνῶσιν ἀληθινήν, καὶ διακρίνω τὰ πάντα.
sentences.e: I consider the knowledge genuine, and I judge all things.

sentences.g: ἴδε, ἃ ποτὲ ἦν παρέρχεται· μιμνῄσκομαι δὲ αὐτῶν.
sentences.e: Behold, what once was passes away; but I remember it.

sentences.g: ἐν τῷ γάμῳ ὁ νυμφίος γεύεται τὸν οἶνον.
sentences.e: At the wedding the bridegroom tastes the wine.

sentences.g: Μαρία καὶ Μαριὰμ φωνοῦσιν· ἥκει ὁ κύριος.
sentences.e: Mary and Mariam call out: the Lord has come.

sentences.g: πόθεν καὶ πόσον; γνωρίζει ὁ θεὸς τὸ μυστήριον.
sentences.e: From where, and how much? God makes the mystery known.

sentences.g: βαστάζει τὸν σταυρόν· ὁ στρατιώτης οὐ νικᾷ αὐτόν.
sentences.e: He bears the cross; the soldier does not overcome him.

sentences.g: ἡ χήρα δέκα ἔτη ἀσθενὴς οὖσα δουλεύει.
sentences.e: The widow, weak for ten years, serves on.

sentences.g: ὁ διάκονος καθαρός ἐστιν καὶ ἀληθής, καὶ συνίει.
sentences.e: The servant is clean and honest, and he understands.

sentences.g: ἕνεκα τῆς ἀδικίας ἐκχέει δάκρυα καὶ λυπεῖ.
sentences.e: On account of the injustice he pours out tears and grieves.

sentences.g: τὸ δένδρον κεῖται· ἄρτι ἀναβλέπω πρὸς τὸν οὐρανόν.
sentences.e: The tree lies fallen; now I look up toward heaven.

sentences.g: Ἰακὼβ καὶ ὁ Ἕλλην προφητεύουσιν πνευματικά.
sentences.e: Jacob and the Greek prophesy spiritual things.

sentences.g: τὸ σόν γε ἔργον φρονεῖς καὶ τελεῖς.
sentences.e: Your own work, at least, you ponder and finish.

sentences.g: ὁ ἁμαρτωλὸς ἄπιστός ἐστιν, ἀλλὰ ἐπιστρέφει καὶ μανθάνει.
sentences.e: The sinner is unbelieving, but he turns back and learns.

sentences.g: ἐν τῷ ἀμπελῶνι αὐξάνει ὁ καρπός· ὁ δὲ δοῦλος καταλείπει αὐτόν.
sentences.e: In the vineyard the fruit grows; but the servant leaves it behind.

sentences.g: Ἠλίας ἀνάγει τὸν παῖδα καὶ ἰᾶται αὐτόν.
sentences.e: Elijah leads the boy up and heals him.

sentences.g: ἡ ἀσθένεια μεγάλη· ἀσθενεῖ γάρ, καὶ οὐκ ἰσχύει.
sentences.e: The sickness is great, for he is weak and is not strong.

sentences.g: ὁ ἀστὴρ λευκὸς ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ φαίνεται ἕκαστον μῆνα.
sentences.e: The star shines white in the cloud each month.

sentences.g: ἡ δέησις καὶ ἡ προσευχὴ πρὸς τὸν θεόν· προσέχομεν οὖν.
sentences.e: The petition and the prayer are toward God; so we pay attention.

sentences.g: ἡ εἰκὼν ἐλευθέρα· μήτε δοῦλος μήποτε αὐτὴν ἀναιρεῖ.
sentences.e: The image is free; and no slave ever destroys it.

sentences.g: ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ πλῆθος πάρεστιν, καὶ ὁ νοῦς πίμπλαται χαρᾶς.
sentences.e: At the festival a multitude is present, and the mind is filled with joy.

sentences.g: Τιμόθεος τὴν ἐπιστολὴν ἀναγινώσκει περὶ τῆς παρουσίας.
sentences.e: Timothy reads the letter about the coming.

sentences.g: κελεύει καὶ προσκαλεῖται αὐτούς· ὀμνύουσιν δὲ φυγεῖν τὴν πορνείαν.
sentences.e: He orders and summons them; and they swear to flee immorality.

sets.name: Nominative
sets.subtitle: The naming case. Who or what the sentence is about.
sets.eli5: This one names people. Nobody here gets hit or eaten. They just get named.
sets.bigIdea: The nominative names. Whoever wears it is being named or called — never done to.
sets.masterMnemonic: Go to the SPA, then say AAAH.
sets.masterMnemonicWhy: SPA is the three main uses: Subject, Predicate nominative, Apposition. AAAH is the other four: Address, Appellation, Absolute, Hanging. Seven uses, one silly picture — you sit down in the spa and go aaah.
sets.scene: Sit in the tub 🛁 — that is SPA — then lie in the steam room 🧖 and say aaah.

groups.name: Major uses — the SPA
groups.mnemonic: S-P-A — sit down in the spa.
groups.expand: Subject · Predicate nominative · Apposition
groups.scene: In the tub: the one in the crown 👑 is doing the verb, a small box 📦 sits inside a bigger one, a ladder 🪜 leans on the wall to settle who is boss, and a name tag 🏷️ is stuck on the towel.

groups.name: Other uses — the AAAH
groups.mnemonic: A-A-A-H — then say aaah.
groups.expand: Address · Appellation · Absolute · Hanging
groups.scene: In the steam room you say aaah: someone calls out 📣, a badge 📛 gives them a title, a headline 📖 hangs over the door tied to nothing, and a knot 🪢 dangles until a pronoun picks it up.

sets.name: Vocative
sets.subtitle: The calling case. One job: naming who you are talking to.
sets.eli5: This one is for shouting a name. “Lazarus!” That is all it does.
sets.bigIdea: The vocative calls. It is the only case with a single use, so it is the cheapest one you will ever learn.
sets.masterMnemonic: One case, one job: say the name.
sets.masterMnemonicWhy: Everything else in the chapter has three, five, seven uses. This one has one. Learn it in ten seconds and spend the time you saved on the accusative.
sets.scene: You stop at one door and shout one name 🗣️. That is the whole stop.

groups.name: Uses of the vocative
groups.mnemonic: Say the name.
groups.expand: Direct address — and that is the list
groups.scene: One man on the doorstep, shouting one name 🗣️. Nothing else lives here.

sets.name: Accusative
sets.subtitle: The fencing case. How far the verb's action goes.
sets.eli5: This one builds a fence. It says where the doing stops.
sets.bigIdea: The accusative fences the verb in. It says how far the action reaches — onto whom, how far, in what way.
sets.masterMnemonic: The object joins the CADETS, then gets the MMR shot.
sets.masterMnemonicWhy: Noun-like: the CADETS — Complement, Alias, Direct object, Echo, Two, Sub. Adverb-like: the MMR shot — Measure, Manner, Respect. How far? How? How so?
sets.scene: Everything happens inside the fence 🚧. In the yard six CADETS 🪖 line up for inspection, then take the MMR jab 💉.

groups.name: The idea
groups.mnemonic: The nominative crowns. The accusative fences.
groups.expand: The nominative crowns. The accusative fences.
groups.scene: The fence 🚧 round the yard. The verb runs until it hits the fence, and that is where the accusative stands.

groups.name: Substantival (noun-like) — CADETS
groups.mnemonic: C-A-D-E-T-S — six cadets line up, and the object is one of them.
groups.expand: Complement (calls it something) · Alias (apposition) · Direct object · Echo (cognate) · Two (person + thing) · Sub (subject of an infinitive)
groups.scene: Six cadets on parade in the yard: one wears a medal 🎖️ that says what he is called, one wears a name tag 🏷️, one holds a glove 🧤 to catch what is thrown, one shouts his own name back 🔁, one 2️⃣ is handed two things at once, and one breaks rank and runs 🏃 — the only one giving orders instead of taking them.

groups.name: Adverbial (adverb-like) — the MMR shot
groups.mnemonic: M-M-R — one shot, three jabs: how far? how? how so?
groups.expand: Measure (how far?) · Manner (how?) · Respect (how so?)
groups.scene: Then the jab, three needles in one shot: a tape measure 📏 for how far, a mask 🎭 for how, a target 🎯 for how so.

sets.name: Genitive
sets.subtitle: The “of” case. The question is always: which kind of “of”?
sets.eli5: This one is the “of” word. “The hat OF Dad.” You just say which kind of “of”.
sets.bigIdea: The genitive describes. The nominative names, the accusative fences, the genitive tells you which kind.
sets.masterMnemonic: Every genitive is an “of”. Ask which kind.
sets.masterMnemonicWhy: Four drawers. Seven describe a noun and spell SWAMP RD — Source, Whole, Adjective, Made of, Possession, Relationship, Description. Two hide a verb: X does it, or X gets it. Five modify a verb and spell PACTS: Price, Agency, Comparison, Time or place, Separation. Then two oddities: another name, and a direct object that came out genitive.
sets.scene: Drive the whole of Swamp Rd 🛣️, stop where the two arrows cross ↔️, sign the PACTS 🤝, and check the odd drawer 🗄️ on the way out.

groups.name: Adjectival — SWAMP RD
groups.mnemonic: S-W-A-M-P R-D — the genitive lives on Swamp Rd, and whatever falls off the end lands in the Ditch. That is Description, the catch-all.
groups.expand: Source (from?) · Whole (part of?) · Adjective (what quality?) · Made of? · Possession (whose?) · Relationship (whose kin?) · Description (nothing else fits)
groups.scene: Drive down Swamp Rd: a spring ⛲ where it came from, a pizza 🍕 you take one slice of, a paintbrush 🖌️ that could just be an adjective, a glass of milk 🥛 for what it is made of, a key 🔑 for who owns it, a father and son 👨‍👦 for kin — and whatever falls off the end lands in the bin 🗑️ at the bottom of the road.

groups.name: Verbal — a verb hiding in the noun
groups.mnemonic: Does it · Gets it — say the head word as a verb and ask which.
groups.expand: Subjective (X does it) · Objective (X gets it)
groups.scene: Where the road crosses, two arrows on one post: ➡️ does it, ⬅️ gets it. Say the head word as a verb and see which way it points.

groups.name: Adverbial — modifies the verb: PACTS
groups.mnemonic: P-A-C-T-S — the adverbial genitive makes PACTS.
groups.expand: Price · Agency · Comparison · Time or place · Separation
groups.scene: At the table where the pacts get signed: money 💰 for the price, a hand ✋ for by whom, scales ⚖️ for than what, a clock 🕐 for when and where, a door 🚪 for away from.

groups.name: Other — the odd drawer
groups.mnemonic: A nickname, and a fussy verb.
groups.expand: Apposition (another name for it) · Direct object (the verb wanted a genitive)
groups.scene: The odd drawer at the end of the road: a name tag 🏷️ for a second name, and a magnet 🧲 for the verbs that pull a genitive object to themselves.

sets.name: Dative
sets.does: gives it, places it, uses it
sets.subtitle: The to/for, in/at, with/by case.
sets.eli5: Three coats on one hook. To or for someone. In or at a place. With or by a thing.
sets.bigIdea: The dative is three old cases wearing one coat: to/for, in/at, with/by. Work out which coat, and the use follows.
sets.masterMnemonicWhy: Three families and a leftover drawer. To or for = PORT. In or at = HIT. With or by = MAMA. Then the odd BEADs.
sets.scene: Sail into PORT ⚓, take the HIT 🥊 on the way up the hill, call on MAMA 👩‍🔧 in her workshop, and string the leftover BEADs 📿.

groups.name: Pure — to or for: PORT
groups.mnemonic: P-O-R-T — and the T, plain “to whom”, is the one you meet most.
groups.expand: Personal interest · Owns (possession) · Re: (reference) · To whom (indirect object)
groups.scene: Down at the port: a heart-wrapped gift 💝 for whose interest it serves, a key 🔑 for who owns it, an envelope ✉️ marked Re: for what it is about, and a parcel 🎁 for who it goes to.

groups.name: Locative — in or at: HIT
groups.mnemonic: H-I-T — Here, In, Then.
groups.expand: Here (place) · In what realm (sphere) · Then (time)
groups.scene: Take the hit on the way up: a pin 📍 for here, a cloud ☁️ for in, a clock 🕐 for then.

groups.name: Instrumental — with or by: MAMA
groups.mnemonic: M-A-M-A — Means, Agency, Manner, Association.
groups.expand: Means (with what tool) · Agency (by whom) · Manner (in what style) · Association (along with)
groups.scene: Mama's workshop: a hammer 🔨 is the tool it was done with, a hand ✋ is the person who did it, a mask 🎭 is the style it was done in, and two friends 👫 came along for the ride.

groups.name: Other — the odd BEADs
groups.mnemonic: B-E-A-D — Because, Echo, Alias, Devoted.
groups.expand: Because (cause) · Echo (cognate) · Alias (apposition) · Devoted verbs (direct object)
groups.scene: Four beads left over on a string: fire 🔥 because, a loop 🔁 echo, a tag 🏷️ alias, hands 🙏 devoted.

sets.name: Article
sets.subtitle: Greek's “the”. It points — and its absence is not “a”.
sets.eli5: Greek's “the” is a finger. It points at one thing. Sometimes it stands in for a word, and sometimes it disappears — and gone does not mean “a”.
sets.bigIdea: The article points. It particularises. And when it is missing, that is information too — not automatically “a”.
sets.masterMnemonicWhy: First the two words: ἄρθρον is a joint, so articular has the article and anarthrous has none. Then three things it does — it Points at something, six ways, and a MAGPIE remembers them; it stands in as a Pronoun in five flavours; or it goes Poof and leaves you three readings to choose between. Then three named rules: Sharp joins, Colwell drops, Apollonius matches.
sets.scene: One finger on a post 👉 with a magpie 🐦 sitting on it, three men 👨‍⚖️ underneath arguing about what it means, and two labels 🦴 nailed to the post naming what is and is not there.

groups.name: The two words for it
groups.mnemonic: ἄρθρον is a joint. With it, articular. Without it, anarthrous.
groups.expand: Articular — the article is there · Anarthrous — it is not
groups.scene: Before you read the post at all, two labels 🦴: a bone with its joint for articular, and a hole 🕳️ where the joint should be for anarthrous.

groups.name: Point — particularising, and generic
groups.mnemonic: M-A-G-P-I-E — a magpie on the signpost, picking out the one shiny thing.
groups.expand: Monadic · Abstract · Generic · Par excellence · Identification · Earlier (anaphoric)
groups.scene: A magpie 🐦 on the post picks out one shiny thing at a time: the only one there is 🌑, the idea itself 💭, the whole class at once 🗂️, the one that deserves the crown 👑, just this one here 🔦, and the one it was talking about a moment ago ↩️.

groups.name: Pronoun — five words it stands in for
groups.mnemonic: They · who · his · those · some…others — five English words, five kinds.
groups.expand: ὁ δέ (he) · ὁ ἐν … (who) · τὸν βίον (his) · οἱ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ (those) · ὁ μέν … ὁ δέ (some … others)
groups.scene: A puzzle piece 🧩 with five shapes: a man 🧔 for he, a chain ⛓️ for who, a briefcase 💼 for his, a finger 👆 for those, and two friends 👬 for some and others.

groups.name: Poof — gone, and gone is not “a”
groups.mnemonic: Ask three things in order: a? the quality? or still THE?
groups.expand: Non-particular — indefinite or qualitative · or definite anyway, in nine standard places
groups.scene: Where the finger vanished 👻, three things it can mean: genuinely “a” 🫥, the quality itself 💎, or still THE 🔒 — and that last one has nine places it happens.

groups.name: Three men, three rules
groups.mnemonic: Sharp joins · Colwell drops · Apollonius matches.
groups.expand: Granville Sharp · Colwell's Rule · Apollonius's Canon
groups.scene: Three men under the post: Sharp holding a chain 🔗 that joins two into one, Colwell with an arrow ⬇️ showing the article dropped off, Apollonius with an equals sign 🟰 — both of them or neither.

sets.name: Adjective
sets.subtitle: Match it, place it. Then four jobs, five degrees.
sets.eli5: A describing word. It can stick to a noun, become the noun, jump to the doing-word, or make a claim. And it comes in degrees: plain, more, most.
sets.bigIdea: First it has to match its noun in case, number and gender. Then look at where the article sits. Then: an adjective does one of four jobs, in one of five degrees.
sets.masterMnemonic: Four jobs ASAP, in five degrees of SPECS.
sets.masterMnemonicWhy: Agreement first — case, number, gender, all three — then position, because where the article sits is what separates attributive from predicate. Only then four jobs, ASAP: Attributive, Substantival, Adverbial, Predicate. Then five degrees, SPECS: Superlative, Positive, Elative, Comparative, Special cases.
sets.scene: Four jobs to do ASAP ⏱️, five strengths of paint you try on through the SPECS 👓 — and a fruit machine 🎰 at the door that will not let you in until case, number and gender line up.

groups.name: Before anything else — match it, then place it
groups.mnemonic: Match it in case, number and gender. Then look at where the article sits.
groups.expand: Agreement — case, number, gender · Position — where the article sits decides attributive or predicate
groups.scene: At the door of the paint shop a fruit machine 🎰 with three reels — case, number, gender — and beside it a compass 🧭 for reading where the article sits. Nothing inside counts until both are done.

groups.name: What it does — ASAP
groups.mnemonic: A-S-A-P — Attributive, Substantival, Adverbial, Predicate.
groups.expand: Sticks to the noun · becomes the noun · jumps to the verb · makes a claim
groups.scene: Four jobs ASAP: a brush 🖌️ sticks the colour to the noun, a figure 🧍 becomes the noun, a kangaroo 🦘 jumps across to the verb, a speech bubble 💬 makes the claim.

groups.name: How strong — SPECS
groups.mnemonic: S-P-E-C-S — Superlative, Positive, Elative, Comparative, Special cases.
groups.expand: The ladder is positive → comparative → superlative. Elative turns the volume up without comparing; special cases swap the three around.
groups.scene: Then try the specs on: a gold medal 🥇 best of the lot, a 1️⃣ plain, a speaker 🔊 that only means “very”, a 2️⃣ more than one other, and a shuffle 🔀 where the forms swap jobs.

sets.name: Person & Number
sets.does: says who is doing it, and how many
sets.subtitle: Six words for who. Three on their own, three in a crowd.
sets.eli5: Who is talking? Me, you, or him. And is it one of them, or a whole crowd?
sets.bigIdea: Three persons, two numbers, six words. Only one pair is dangerous: ἡμεῖς is “we” and ὑμεῖς is “you all”, and they are one letter apart.
sets.masterMnemonic: I, you, he — then all of us, all of you, all of them.
sets.masterMnemonicWhy: Say the roll call out loud in that order and the whole table is done. The Greek verb ending already tells you which one, so the pronoun is usually there for emphasis.
sets.scene: Six people answer to their names at the door 🙋 — three on their own, three in a crowd.

groups.name: The roll call
groups.key: I · You · He · We · You all · They
groups.mnemonic: I, you, he — then we, you all, they.
groups.expand: ἐγώ · σύ · αὐτός — ἡμεῖς · ὑμεῖς · αὐτοί
groups.scene: Six answer the roll: 🙋 ἐγώ (my hand goes up), 👤 σύ (the one I am looking at), 🚗 αὐτός — an AUTO drives itSELF — then 🫂 ἡμεῖς (my lot), 👥 ὑμεῖς (your lot), 🚙 αὐτοί (their autos). The trap is the middle pair: ὑ has the u of YOU.

sets.name: Voice
sets.does: aims the action out, back, or in
sets.subtitle: How much of the action lands back on the subject.
sets.eli5: Who is doing it, and does it come back? I do it. I do it to me. It gets done to me.
sets.bigIdea: Three voices, one question: how much of this lands back on the subject? Active none, middle some, passive all.
sets.masterMnemonic: I do it · I do it for me · It is done to me.
sets.masterMnemonicWhy: Active points out, middle bends back, passive comes in. Say those three lines in order and the voices sort themselves before you look at a single ending.
sets.scene: Three faders on the desk 🎙️: push it out 💪 (active), bend it back 🪞 (middle), let it come in 📥 (passive).

groups.name: Active — it points out
groups.mnemonic: Do it · Make it happen · Do it to me.
groups.expand: Simple (he does it) · Causative (he makes it happen) · Reflexive (he does it to himself, with a pronoun)
groups.scene: Push the fader out 💪: one just does it ⚡, one makes the sun come up 🌅 without lifting a finger, and one trains himself 🏋️ — active verb, reflexive pronoun.

groups.name: Middle — it bends back
groups.key: To me · For me · Let me
groups.mnemonic: To me · For me · Let me — the middle always has the subject in it.
groups.expand: Reflexive (to himself) · Special interest (for himself) · Permissive (he lets it be done to him)
groups.scene: Everything thrown at the mirror 🪞 comes back: a boomerang 🪃 to himself, a basket 🛒 he filled for himself, and open hands 🤲 letting it be done to him.

groups.name: Passive — it comes in
groups.key: Done to me · Let it be done
groups.mnemonic: Done to me · Let it be done.
groups.expand: Simple (he receives it) · Permissive (he consents to it)
groups.scene: Two things land in the tray 📥: one arrives whether he likes it or not 📥, and one he opens the door to 🕊️.

sets.name: Mood
sets.does: frames it as fact, maybe, order or wish
sets.subtitle: How real the speaker says it is — and whether he is telling you to do it.
sets.eli5: Is it a fact, a maybe, an order, or a wish? That is all mood is. Indicative: it happened. Subjunctive: it might. Imperative: do it. Optative: I hope so.
sets.bigIdea: Mood is the weather of the sentence. Clear sky ☀️ for what is, fog 🌫️ for what might be, thunder ⛈️ for do it, a rainbow 🌈 for I wish.
sets.masterMnemonic: It is · It might · Do it · I wish.
sets.masterMnemonicWhy: Four moods, four postures. Indicative states, subjunctive supposes, imperative orders, optative wishes. Name the posture first and the use is a short list after that.
sets.scene: Four dials on the wall 🌦️: clear sky ☀️ it is, fog 🌫️ it might be, thunder ⛈️ do it, rainbow 🌈 I wish.

groups.name: Indicative — clear sky, it is so
groups.mnemonic: W-A-I-F-S — five waifs turn up at the station.
groups.expand: Want (potential) · Ask (interrogative) · If (conditional) · Fact (declarative) · Shall (cohortative)
groups.scene: Five waifs at the weather station, and every one of them speaks in plain fact: one Wants 💭, one Asks ❓, one says If 🚦, one reads out the Fact 📰, and one says you Shall 📜.

groups.name: Subjunctive after a word — it might be
groups.mnemonic: Five little words pull a subjunctive: ἵνα, ἵνα, ἐάν, ὃς ἄν, ὅταν.
groups.expand: Purpose (aim) · Result (outcome) · Conditional (if) · Indefinite relative (whoever) · Indefinite temporal (whenever)
groups.scene: Out in the fog you cannot see the verb, only the word in front of it: an arrow 🏹 for what was aimed at, a bang 💥 for what actually came of it, dice 🎲 for if, a ticket 🎟️ for whoever, an alarm clock ⏰ for whenever.

groups.name: Subjunctive on its own — no word in front
groups.key: Let us · Should we · Never · Don't
groups.mnemonic: Let us · Should we · Never · Don't — four things you can say with no ἵνα in sight.
groups.expand: Hortatory (let us) · Deliberative (should we?) · Emphatic negation (οὐ μή, never) · Prohibitory (μή + aorist, don't)
groups.scene: A gust blows the fog off 🌬️ and the subjunctive speaks for itself: hands up 🙌 “let us”, a raised eyebrow 🤔 “should we?”, a hard no 🚫 “never”, and a flat palm 🙅 “don't”.

groups.name: Imperative — thunder, do it
groups.mnemonic: P-H-O-N-I-C — six things you say out loud.
groups.expand: Please (request) · Hi (greeting) · OK (permission) · No (prohibition) · If (conditional) · Charge (command)
groups.scene: Six things shouted through the thunder ⛈️: Please 🙇 to somebody above you, Hi 👋 in passing, OK 👌 letting it go, No ❌ forbidding it, If 👣 — come and see — and the plain Charge 🫡.

groups.name: Optative — a rainbow, I wish
groups.mnemonic: May · Might · Should — three English words, three optative uses.
groups.expand: Voluntative (may it be) · Deliberative (what it might be) · Potential (if you should)
groups.scene: A rainbow 🌈 over the station, and three wishes under it: a candle 🕯️ “may grace be multiplied”, a puzzled question ❔ “what might this mean?”, and a four-leaf clover 🍀 for the fourth class — “even if you should suffer”.

sets.name: Tense
sets.does: says when, and how it is being pictured
sets.subtitle: Six forms of λύω, and the three marks that give them away.
sets.eli5: When did it happen, and are we watching it happen or just told that it did?
sets.bigIdea: Three marks decode the whole table. An ἐ- on the front means past. A σ after the stem means future or aorist. The stem said twice means perfect.
sets.masterMnemonic: Am · Will · Was · Did · Have · Had.
sets.masterMnemonicWhy: Six English helpers, six Greek forms, in the chart's own order. The book flags the catch itself: “It should be noted that this chart is an oversimplification of the wide diversity of tense-form uses and that students will not always translate verbs in such a manner.”
sets.scene: Six bells in the tower ⏳, and three tell-tales chalked on the wall: ἐ- means past, σ means future or aorist, and the stem said twice means perfect.

groups.name: The six forms of λύω
groups.key: Am · Will · Was · Did · Have · Had
groups.mnemonic: Am · Will · Was · Did · Have · Had — say the English helper and the Greek form follows.
groups.expand: λύω · λύσω · ἔλυον · ἔλυσα · λέλυκα · ἐλελύκειν
groups.scene: Six bells, one after another 🎬 I am loosing, 🔮 I will loose, 🎞️ I was loosing, 📸 I loosed, 🧱 I have loosed, 🕰️ I had loosed. Read the marks, not the meaning: ἐ- past, σ future or aorist, doubled stem perfect.

cards.name: Subject
cards.eli5: Who is doing it. “John talks.” Who talks? John.
cards.oneLine: The one doing the verb.
cards.mnemonic: The subject wears the crown.
cards.mnemonicWhy: The nominative names, and the crown sits on whoever the verb is about. One verb, one nominative — that one is wearing it.
cards.spotIt: Ask the verb: who or what? That is your subject.
cards.bookDef: The subject of a finite verb.

examples.note: John is nominative and does the witnessing. As plain as it gets.
One verb, one nominative. Nothing tricky.

cards.name: Predicate Nominative
cards.eli5: “X is Y” puts X inside Y, like a box. The Word goes in the God box. Not the other way round.
cards.oneLine: Two nominatives with “is” between them. The second says what the first is.
cards.mnemonic: The subject is the small circle; the predicate is the big one.
cards.mnemonicWhy: “Is” looks like an equals sign, but it only points one way. “The Word was God” puts the Word inside God, not God inside the Word. Small circle inside a big one.
cards.spotIt: Find a form of “to be” — εἰμί, γίνομαι, ὑπάρχω — with a nominative on each side of it.
cards.bookDef: Provides further information about the subject as a complement of a copulative verb (expressing a state of being).
cards.watchOut: Apposition looks the same but has no verb. A verb makes a claim. A comma only makes a label.

examples.note: ὁ λόγος has the article, so it is the subject. θεός is what is said about it.
ὁ θεός has the article, so it is the subject. Love is what is said about him.
αὐτός is a pronoun, so it takes the subject slot. See the pecking order.
ἐγένετο is a “became” verb, which counts. σάρξ is what is said about the Word.

cards.name: The Pecking Order
cards.eli5: Two words both look like the doer. Pick like picking teams: “he” words first, then “the” words, then names.

formula.note: First yes wins. John 1:1c: no pronoun, ὁ λόγος has the article — so it is the subject.

cards.oneLine: Two nominatives, one “is”. This is how you tell which one is the subject.
cards.mnemonic: PAP — ask Papa who is in charge.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Pronoun, then Article, then Proper name. Papa answers in that order every time.
cards.spotIt: Go down the list and stop at the first yes.
cards.watchOut: No article does not mean “a”. A predicate noun sitting in front of the verb normally drops it.

examples.note: No pronoun, so the article decides: ὁ λόγος has it and is the subject, which makes θεός the predicate. Not “a god” — Greek can be perfectly definite with no article.
αὐτός is a pronoun, so it wins — even though ἡ εἰρήνη has the article.

cards.name: Apposition
cards.eli5: Same person, two stickers. “Andrew, Peter’s brother.” No “is” — just a second sticker.

formula.note: No verb anywhere.

cards.oneLine: Two nominatives side by side, no verb. The second renames the first.
cards.mnemonic: No verb, just a name tag.
cards.mnemonicWhy: A sticker slapped on the first word: “Andrew — HELLO MY NAME IS the brother of Simon Peter.” Nothing is claimed; he is just being identified.
cards.spotIt: Two nominatives, a pause between them, and no “is” anywhere.
cards.bookDef: Further explains the subject by clarification, description, or identification.
cards.watchOut: The only difference from a predicate nominative is the verb. Comma = label. “Is” = claim. And watch the chart: Rom 1:1 is filed here because δοῦλος explains Παῦλος, while the near-identical Titus 1:1 is filed under absolute because there the whole salutation stands alone.

examples.note: ἀδελφός renames Andrew. Nothing is being claimed about him.
δοῦλος renames Paul.
A name tag. Compare “Ivan is the student” — that one has a verb, so it is a claim.

cards.name: Nominative of Address
cards.eli5: “Hey, Dad!” You are talking TO him, not about him.
cards.oneLine: A nominative used to call out to someone.
cards.mnemonic: "Hey, you!" in a nominative coat.
cards.mnemonicWhy: He is being spoken to, not described. It looks like a subject and works like a shout.
cards.spotIt: Try an exclamation mark after it. “Husbands! — love your wives.” If that works, it is address.
cards.bookDef: Used in the place of a vocative in direct address.
cards.watchOut: A subject is talked about. An address is talked to. Same case, opposite direction.

examples.english: Have mercy on us, *Son of David*
examples.note: He is being called out to, not described. Nominative shape, vocative job.
Not a statement about husbands. A shout at them.

cards.name: Nominative of Appellation
cards.eli5: It is the name on his badge. Everyone says “Teacher”, so that became his name.
cards.gist: a title used as a name

formula.note: X stays nominative.

cards.oneLine: A title used as somebody's name, left in the nominative.
cards.mnemonic: The title is on the name badge — and badges don't decline.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Once “Teacher” is what people call him, it stops behaving like a word in a sentence and behaves like the name printed on a badge.
cards.spotIt: It is a title, it is what someone is called, and it stayed nominative when the sentence wanted an accusative.
cards.bookDef: Used in conjunction with an address or title where a case other than the nominative would be expected.
cards.watchOut: The easiest of the four. If a nominative is plainly a title-as-name, stop looking for something cleverer.

examples.greek: ὑμεῖς φωνεῖτέ με *ὁ διδάσκαλος* καὶ *ὁ κύριος*
examples.note: φωνεῖτέ με wants an accusative after it. The titles stay nominative because they are the name.

cards.name: Nominative Absolute
cards.eli5: It is the title on the front of a book. It sits on top and joins nothing.
cards.oneLine: A nominative attached to nothing — a heading or a greeting.
cards.mnemonic: Absolute = the headline.
cards.mnemonicWhy: A headline floats above the page, tied to nothing. No verb, no clause, no rope.
cards.spotIt: Opening material — a title, a greeting, a list — with no verb to hook it to.
cards.bookDef: Grammatically independent use of the nominative in introductory material (such as titles, headings, salutations, or addresses).
cards.watchOut: No rope at all. If a pronoun later picks the word back up, it is hanging, not absolute.

examples.english: *The beginning* of the gospel of Jesus Christ
examples.note: ἀρχή is nominative and stands completely alone. Everything hanging off it is genitive.

examples.english: *Grace, mercy, peace* from God the Father
examples.note: All nominative, all opening material, all tied to nothing.
The whole salutation stands alone, and Παῦλος is the word left hanging. Compare Rom 1:1, where the same phrase is filed under apposition.

cards.name: Hanging Nominative
cards.eli5: You say the thing, then point back at it. “The good seed? THOSE are the king’s kids.”
cards.oneLine: A loose nominative that a pronoun picks up later.
cards.mnemonic: It hangs by a pronoun.
cards.mnemonicWhy: The pronoun downstream is the rope. Cut it and the word drops — which is exactly what an absolute never had.
cards.spotIt: Find the loose nominative, then look ahead for the pronoun standing in its place.
cards.bookDef: The logical rather than syntactical subject at the beginning of a sentence.
cards.watchOut: Absolute = no connection. Hanging = connected in sense, but not in grammar.

examples.greek: τὸ δὲ καλὸν *σπέρμα*, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας
examples.english: and the good *seed* — these are the sons of the kingdom
examples.note: σπέρμα is left dangling, but οὗτοι (“these”) does its job in the main clause. That pronoun is the rope.

examples.greek: *ὁ νικῶν* ποιήσω αὐτὸν στῦλον ἐν τῷ ναῷ τοῦ θεοῦ μου
examples.english: *The one who conquers*, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God
examples.note: ὁ νικῶν is left dangling, and αὐτόν picks it up. That pronoun is the rope.

cards.name: Direct Address
cards.eli5: You call his name. “Lazarus, come out!” The name is just how you got him to look.

formula.note: The name is not the doer. It is who you are shouting at.

cards.oneLine: Naming the person or thing you are speaking to.
cards.mnemonic: Say the name, then say the thing.
cards.mnemonicWhy: The whole case is one move: get their attention, then tell them. With or without “the” in front — the chart allows both.
cards.spotIt: Somebody is being called by name or title, and that word is not doing any work in the sentence.
cards.bookDef: The use of the articular or non-articular vocative to designate the person or thing being addressed.
cards.watchOut: When a word does this job but is shaped like a nominative, the chart calls it nominative of address instead. Same job, different clothes.

examples.note: He is being called, not described. That is the vocative’s only job.

cards.name: The Case of Limitation
cards.eli5: Doing-words need a fence. This builds it. The doing stops here.
cards.oneLine: The accusative fences the verb in — it says how far the action goes.
cards.mnemonic: The nominative crowns; the accusative fences.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Every use is a fence post: onto whom (object), how far (measure), in what way (manner), about what (respect).
cards.spotIt: Two families. Does it act like a noun, or like an adverb?

examples.ref: The whole chapter in one line
examples.english: One object with four twists — Echo, Two, Sub, Alias — then the MMR shot: Measure, Manner, Respect.
examples.note: Noun-like first, adverb-like second.

cards.name: Double Accusative — Object and Complement
cards.eli5: You call the thing a name. “He gave his life AS a ransom.” The word “as” slips right in.

formula.note: Both are accusative. The second one is not a second victim — it is a label.

cards.oneLine: Two accusatives, where the second says what the first is called or made.
cards.mnemonic: CADETS — C: complement, you Call it something.
cards.mnemonicWhy: One test, one word: put “as” between the two accusatives. “His life AS a ransom.” “You AS friends.” If “as” fits, the second one is the complement.
cards.spotIt: Two accusatives with no “and” between them, and “as” slips in: object + complement.
cards.bookDef: A verb requires more than one accusative object to complete the thought, taking either (1) a personal and impersonal object or (2) a direct and predicate object.
cards.watchOut: Not apposition. Apposition renames something by what it already is; a complement says what it is being called, made or given as — and there is a verb doing the calling.

examples.english: to give his *life* as a *ransom* for many
examples.note: life is the object, ransom is what it was given as. “As” slips right in.

examples.english: I no longer call *you* *servants* … but I have called *you* *friends*
examples.note: Same construction twice in one verse. You are the object; servants and friends are what you get called.

examples.english: who gave *himself* as *a ransom* for all
examples.note: himself is the object, ransom is the label.

cards.name: Accusative of Apposition
cards.eli5: Two stickers again, on the catcher. “They picked Stephen, a good man.”
cards.oneLine: A second accusative that renames the first. No verb between them.
cards.mnemonic: CADETS — A: alias, the name tag on the object.
cards.mnemonicWhy: The same sticker you met in the nominative, now stuck on the catcher.
cards.spotIt: Two accusatives, no verb between them, and the second answers “which one, exactly?”
cards.bookDef: Two accusatives are juxtaposed, both referring to the same person or thing, with the second accusative further specifying the first accusative.
cards.watchOut: Not a complement. Apposition has no verb doing the naming: the two words simply sit side by side and the second one says which one, exactly.

examples.english: they chose Stephen, *a man* full of faith
examples.note: Stephen is the object; “a man” renames him.
Israel renames “my people”.

examples.english: and on a colt, *the foal* of a donkey
examples.note: υἱόν renames πῶλον. One animal, two names.

cards.name: Direct Object
cards.eli5: This is the catcher. “I hit Ivan.” Ivan got hit.
cards.oneLine: What the verb lands on. By far the most common one.
cards.mnemonic: CADETS — D: the verb throws, the object catches.
cards.mnemonicWhy: The plain one, and the trunk the other four grow off. Get this solid first.
cards.spotIt: After the verb, ask: whom? what?
cards.bookDef: Serves as the recipient of the action.
cards.watchOut: A few verbs take their object in the genitive or the dative instead — ἀκούω, κρατέω, προσκυνέω. The case follows the verb, not the meaning.

examples.note: Ivan catches the hitting.

examples.greek: οὕτως γὰρ ἠγάπησεν ὁ θεὸς *τὸν κόσμον*
examples.note: The world is what the loving lands on.
Ask the verb “whom?” and the accusative answers.

cards.name: Cognate Accusative
cards.eli5: The word says the doing-word again. “Sing a song.” “Fight a fight.”
cards.oneLine: An object that repeats the verb — same root, or same idea.
cards.mnemonic: CADETS — E: echo, the object repeats the verb.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Say the verb and hear it come straight back: sing a song, fight a fight, shepherd a flock.
cards.spotIt: Say the verb and the object out loud. Sounds redundant in English? Cognate.
cards.bookDef: Aligned with the verb either with regard to the lexical root or the idea conveyed.
cards.watchOut: Still the direct object. “Cognate” only names the flavour.

examples.note: The same root twice — the tightest echo there is.
ἐχάρησαν and χαράν are the same root. The echo is the whole point — it turns the volume up.
Not the same root, but the same idea. That counts too.
The textbook one.

cards.name: Double Accusative — Person and Thing
cards.eli5: Two catchers, and one of them is a person. “Ask Dad for bread.” Dad and bread both catch it.

formula.note: Both are accusative. Neither one is a label — they are two real objects.

cards.oneLine: Two accusatives: somebody, and the thing done to them.
cards.mnemonic: CADETS — T: two catchers, a person and a thing.
cards.mnemonicWhy: You ASK a person FOR a thing. You TEACH a person A LESSON. Two objects, and “as” will not go between them — “asks him as bread” is nonsense.
cards.spotIt: Two accusatives, one of them a person, and “as” will not fit between them.
cards.bookDef: A verb requires more than one accusative object to complete the thought, taking either (1) a personal and impersonal object or (2) a direct and predicate object.
cards.watchOut: The usual verbs are asking, teaching, reminding, clothing and anointing — verbs that naturally take somebody and something.

examples.note: him (a person) + bread (a thing). “Asks him as bread” is nonsense, so it is not a complement.
you (person) + all things (thing). Teaching verbs do this constantly.
Two objects, no label. The class is not “being called” Greek.

cards.name: Accusative Subject of the Infinitive
cards.eli5: Usually this one catches the ball. Not here — here it throws. “I want HIM to go.” He is the one going.

formula.note: X is accusative — and X is the one doing it.

cards.oneLine: An infinitive's subject is accusative, not nominative.
cards.mnemonic: CADETS — S: sub, the infinitive's own subject.
cards.mnemonicWhy: The odd one out — this accusative is doing the action, not catching it.
cards.spotIt: Find the infinitive, then the accusative that is doing it rather than receiving it.
cards.bookDef: Functions as the subject of an infinitive, indicating the agent performing the action conveyed by the infinitive.
cards.watchOut: The only accusative you translate as the doer — and only when there is an infinitive for it to be the subject of. No infinitive, no sub.

examples.note: “Him” is the one going. In Greek that word is accusative.

examples.greek: πρὸ τοῦ σε *Φίλιππον* φωνῆσαι … εἶδόν σε
examples.english: Before *Philip* called you … I saw you
examples.note: φωνῆσαι is the infinitive, and Philip is the one doing the calling — accusative, but the doer.
Careful — this one is a plain object, not a subject. There is no infinitive for it to be the subject of.

cards.name: Accusative of Measure
cards.eli5: How far? How long? “He walked a little bit.”
cards.oneLine: How far, how long, how much.
cards.mnemonic: MMR, shot one: How far?
cards.mnemonicWhy: The MMR shot, one of three. This is the one with a tape measure on it.
cards.spotIt: Ask: how far? how long? Does the accusative answer?
cards.bookDef: Functions in essence like an adverb in that it specifies measure (time or space).

examples.greek: καὶ προσελθὼν *μικρόν*, ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ
examples.english: And going *a little farther* he fell on his face
examples.note: μικρόν measures the distance. It is not the object of anything.

cards.name: Accusative of Manner
cards.eli5: How did you do it? “He gave it for free.”
cards.oneLine: How the action is done.
cards.mnemonic: MMR, shot two: How?
cards.mnemonicWhy: The MMR shot, two of three. It turns a noun into an adverb: δωρεάν stops being “a gift” and becomes “freely”.
cards.spotIt: Ask: how? Check that an -ly word is the natural English.
cards.bookDef: Functions in essence like an adverb in that it specifies manner.

examples.note: δωρεάν = freely, as a gift. It describes how the justifying happened.

cards.name: Accusative of Respect
cards.eli5: Only one part of you is meant. “Cut to the heart” — the heart is the part that hurt, not your skin.
cards.oneLine: In one way only — put “with respect to” in front of it.
cards.mnemonic: MMR, shot three: How so? — slot in "as to".
cards.mnemonicWhy: The MMR shot, three of three, and the narrowest fence. The verb happened, but only in one respect, and this names which.
cards.spotIt: Say it with “with respect to” in front. If that rescues the sense, this is it.
cards.bookDef: Restricts the reference of the verbal action, indicating in what regard an action is represented as true.
cards.watchOut: Easy to mistake for the object. If “with respect to” makes it better, it is respect.

examples.english: they were pierced *with respect to the heart*
examples.note: Not a surgical piercing — an inner one. “With respect to” is what keeps it from sounding like an operation.

examples.english: When they heard this, they were pierced *to the heart*
examples.note: The book spells the sense out: “they were pierced with reference to the heart.”

cards.name: Source
cards.eli5: It flowed out of that. “Righteousness of God” means righteousness FROM God.

formula.note: = that comes FROM X.

cards.oneLine: Where the head word came from.
cards.mnemonic: SWAMP RD — S: where it came from.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Swap “of” for “from” and see whether it still works. “The righteousness from God.”
cards.spotIt: Try “from” in place of “of”. Still makes sense? Source.
cards.bookDef: Indicates the origin of the head noun (“from”).
cards.watchOut: Separation also translates “from”. Source is where a noun came from; separation is what a verb moves away from.

examples.note: The righteousness comes from God. Swap in “from” and it still reads.

cards.name: Partitive
cards.eli5: The “of” word is the big pile. The other word is your piece. “One of the boats.”

formula.note: The genitive is the WHOLE. The head noun is the part.

cards.oneLine: The genitive is the whole; the head word is a piece of it.
cards.mnemonic: SWAMP RD — W: the genitive is the whole pie, the head word your slice.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Backwards from what you expect: the word in the genitive is the bigger thing, not the smaller one.
cards.spotIt: Ask: is the genitive word the whole that the other word is a piece of?
cards.bookDef: Whether by itself or in conjunction with the preposition ἀπό or ἐκ, the articular noun in the genitive denotes the whole of which the head noun is a part.
cards.watchOut: Often turns up with ἀπό or ἐκ, and the genitive noun carries the article.

examples.note: The boats are the whole; the one boat is the part.

cards.name: Attributive
cards.eli5: “The word of his power” really means “his POWERFUL word.” Squish it into a describing word.

formula.note: → his POWERFUL word. X becomes the adjective.

cards.oneLine: A quality of the head word — it could have been an adjective.
cards.mnemonic: SWAMP RD — A: turn the genitive into an adjective.
cards.mnemonicWhy: “The word of his power” → “his powerful word.” If the genitive can become the adjective, and saying it that way is stronger, it is attributive.
cards.spotIt: Try rewriting the genitive as an adjective in front of the head noun. Does it work?
cards.bookDef: Denotes an attribute or innate quality of the head term, conveying an emphatic adjectival idea.
cards.watchOut: Description is the vaguer cousin. Attributive earns its name because the genitive really does become an adjective.

examples.note: “Word of power” becomes “powerful word”. That rewrite is the test.

cards.name: Material or Content
cards.eli5: What it is made of, or what is in it. “A cup of water” is full of water.
cards.gist: Made of it, full of it

formula.note: = made of X, or full of X.

cards.oneLine: What it is made of, or what is inside it.
cards.mnemonic: SWAMP RD — M: made of it, or full of it.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Cargo of gold is made of gold. A cup of water is full of water. One case, two flavours.
cards.spotIt: Ask: made of what? or full of what?
cards.bookDef: Indicates the material of which the head term is made or specifies the content of an object or abstract noun.

examples.note: Material — the cargo is made of gold.
Content — the cup is full of water.

cards.name: Possession
cards.eli5: It is his. “The house of Philip” means Philip’s house.

formula.note: = X’s. Try the apostrophe-s.

cards.oneLine: It belongs to X.
cards.mnemonic: SWAMP RD — P: whose? Try the apostrophe-s.
cards.mnemonicWhy: “The house of Philip” → “Philip’s house.” If the apostrophe-s works and means he owns it, it is possession.
cards.spotIt: Rewrite it with ’s. Does it mean he owns the thing?
cards.bookDef: Identifies ownership with regard to the noun it modifies, often employing the use of a possessive pronoun.
cards.watchOut: Relationship takes an apostrophe-s too — “Zebedee’s son”. Owning a thing is possession; family is relationship.

examples.note: Philip’s house. He owns it.

cards.name: Relationship
cards.eli5: It is family, and Greek left the family word out. “James of Zebedee” means Zebedee’s son.

formula.note: → James, the SON of Zebedee. The kin word is missing.

cards.oneLine: X’s son, wife or parent — with the family word left out.
cards.mnemonic: SWAMP RD — R: supply the missing kin word.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Greek leaves out “son” or “wife” and expects you to know. Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου is “James the [son] of Zebedee.”
cards.spotIt: A name in the genitive with no thing to own? Try slotting in “son of” or “wife of”.
cards.bookDef: Denotes a family relationship such as a person’s parent or spouse. The word indicating the relationship is often omitted and must be inferred.
cards.watchOut: Possession is owning a thing. Relationship is family, with the kin word usually left out.

examples.note: “Son” is nowhere in the Greek. You supply it.

cards.name: Description
cards.eli5: The leftovers bin. Nobody owns it, it is not made of it — it just describes.

formula.note: Nothing more specific fits.

cards.oneLine: It describes the head word, and nothing more specific fits.
cards.mnemonic: SWAMP RD — D: the ditch at the end of the road.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Walk the ladder first. When nothing more specific fits, this catches it. A baptism of repentance is not owned by repentance, not made of it — just described by it.
cards.spotIt: Run the ladder. If no other category fits, it is description.
cards.bookDef: Further limits or describes the head noun, but other common genitival categories do not capture the specific nuance.
cards.watchOut: Do not reach for this first. It is the bottom of the ladder, not the top.

examples.note: Not possessed, not made of, not from. Just described.

cards.name: Subjective
cards.eli5: The “of” word is doing it. “The love of Christ” — Christ is doing the loving.

formula.note: → Christ loves. X does the action.

cards.oneLine: X is doing the action hidden in the head word.
cards.mnemonic: Subject does it.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Turn the head noun back into a verb. “The love of Christ” → Christ loves. X is the one doing it.
cards.spotIt: Make the head noun a verb, then ask: is X doing it?
cards.bookDef: Functions semantically as the subject of the verbal idea implied in the head noun, producing the action.

examples.greek: τίς ἡμᾶς χωρίσει ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης *τοῦ Χριστοῦ*;
examples.english: Who can separate us from the love *of Christ*?
examples.note: Christ is the one loving. Make the noun a verb and X is doing it.

cards.name: Objective
cards.eli5: The “of” word is getting it. “Faith of God” means faith IN God.

formula.note: → you believe God. X receives the action.

cards.oneLine: X is receiving the action hidden in the head word.
cards.mnemonic: Object gets it.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Same move, other direction. “Faith of God” means faith IN God — God is on the receiving end.
cards.spotIt: Make the head noun a verb, then ask: is X getting it?
cards.bookDef: Functions semantically as the direct object of the verbal idea implicit in the head noun, receiving the action.
cards.watchOut: Subjective and objective look identical in Greek. Only the sense decides which one it is.

examples.note: God is believed in, not believing. X is receiving the action.

cards.name: Price
cards.eli5: How much did it cost? “Bought with a price.”

formula.note: for how much?

cards.oneLine: What it cost, or what it is worth.
cards.mnemonic: PACTS — P: for how much?
cards.mnemonicWhy: PACTS opens with the price, because the first thing any pact settles is what it costs. ἠγοράσθητε τιμῆς — you were bought at a price.
cards.spotIt: Ask: at what price? worth how much?
cards.bookDef: Indicates the price that is paid or the value that attaches to a given item.

examples.english: you have been bought *with a price*
examples.note: τιμῆς is what was paid.

cards.name: Means or Agency
cards.eli5: Who did it, or what did it. “Blessed BY my Father” — Dad did the blessing.

formula.note: by what? by whom?

cards.oneLine: By what, or by whom, the action was done.
cards.mnemonic: PACTS — A: by what? by whom?
cards.mnemonicWhy: A thing did it (means) or a person did it (agency). Both come out as “by”.
cards.spotIt: Ask: by what, or by whom? A thing = means. A person = agency.
cards.bookDef: Conveys the impersonal means or personal agent by which a given action is carried out (“by”).

examples.english: Since God is not tempted *by evil*
examples.note: Means — evil is a thing, not a person.

examples.english: Come, you who are blessed *by my Father*
examples.note: Agency — the Father is a person.

cards.name: Comparison
cards.eli5: This is the thing being beaten. “God is greater THAN our heart” — the heart is what he beat.

formula.note: than what?

cards.oneLine: What something is being measured against.
cards.mnemonic: PACTS — C: than what?
cards.mnemonicWhy: Find a comparative — greater, better, more — and the genitive beside it is the thing being beaten.
cards.spotIt: See a comparative adjective? The genitive next to it is the “than”.
cards.bookDef: Used to denote comparison in conjunction with a comparative adjective (“than”).

examples.greek: μείζων ἐστὶν ὁ θεὸς *τῆς καρδίας* ἡμῶν
examples.note: μείζων is the comparative; the genitive is what he is greater than.

cards.name: Time or Place
cards.eli5: When it happened, or where. “He came AT NIGHT” — night is the when.

formula.note: when? where?

cards.oneLine: When or where the action happened.
cards.mnemonic: PACTS — T: when? where?
cards.mnemonicWhy: The one with a clock and a map on it. Note the focus is the kind of time, not a point on a clock.
cards.spotIt: Ask: when did it happen? where did it happen?
cards.bookDef: Indicates the location in time or space where an action occurs. The focus is on kind or quality.

examples.greek: ὁ ἐλθὼν πρὸς αὐτὸν *νυκτὸς* τὸ πρῶτον
examples.english: who had previously come to him *at night*
examples.note: Time — night is the kind of time it happened in.
Place — where the exile went.

cards.name: Separation
cards.eli5: Moving away. “They walked away from the faith.”

formula.note: away from what?

cards.oneLine: What the action moves away from.
cards.mnemonic: PACTS — S: away from what?
cards.mnemonicWhy: Movement away, real or figurative — walking away from a place, or away from the faith.
cards.spotIt: Ask: away from what? Does “from” fit?
cards.bookDef: Indicates motion away from or distance, whether literally or figuratively (“from”).
cards.watchOut: Source also translates “from”. Separation moves away from something; source is where a noun came from.

examples.note: Movement away from — figurative, but still away.

cards.name: Apposition
cards.eli5: Two stickers, third time. “Jeremiah the prophet.” One man, two names.

formula.note: X is another name for the head noun.

cards.oneLine: A second name for the head word.
cards.mnemonic: The name tag again — third case running.
cards.mnemonicWhy: You have met this in the nominative and the accusative. Same move: the second word renames the first.
cards.spotIt: Ask: is the genitive another name for the head noun? “Jeremiah, who is the prophet.” “The gift, which is the Holy Spirit.”
cards.bookDef: The genitive of apposition provides an alternate designation (simple) of a genitive head noun or provides an explanatory (epexegetical) restatement of a head noun in any case.
cards.watchOut: Simple: the head noun is genitive too. Epexegetical: the head noun can be any case.

examples.note: Simple — the head noun Ἰερεμίου is itself genitive.
Epexegetical — the gift IS the Spirit. The head noun here is accusative.

cards.name: Direct Object
cards.eli5: Some doing-words are picky. Hearing, wanting, sharing, bossing and leaving all want their catcher dressed like this.

formula.note: The verb wanted a genitive, not an accusative.

cards.oneLine: The object of a verb that wants the genitive instead of the accusative.
cards.mnemonic: Feel it, want it, share it, rule it, leave it.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Six kinds of verb do this: sensation and emotion (feel it), volition (want it), sharing, ruling, separation (leave it). It is a habit of the verb, not a meaning.
cards.spotIt: A genitive sitting where you expected an accusative? Check the verb: sensing, feeling, wanting, sharing, ruling, separating?
cards.bookDef: Verbs of sensation, emotion or volition, sharing, ruling, or separation take their direct object in the genitive case (instead of the accusative case).
cards.watchOut: This one follows a VERB. The objective genitive follows a NOUN.

examples.english: you did not lack *anything*, did you?
examples.note: ὑστερέω takes its object in the genitive.

examples.greek: οἱ νεκροὶ ἀκούσουσιν *τῆς φωνῆς* τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ
examples.english: the dead will hear *the voice* of the Son of God
examples.note: Sensation — hearing. Feel it.

examples.english: I have not coveted anyone’s *silver* or *gold* or *clothing*
examples.note: Emotion and volition — coveting. Want it.

examples.english: You cannot share in the Lord’s *table*
examples.note: Sharing. Share it.

examples.english: For sin will not rule over *you*
examples.note: Ruling. Rule it.

cards.name: Personal Interest
cards.eli5: Someone gains, or someone loses. “A bride dressed up FOR her husband.” “She had it IN for him.”

formula.note: Good for X, or bad for X.

cards.oneLine: Who benefits, or who suffers.
cards.mnemonic: PORT — P: for him, or against him.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Two directions, one use. Rev 21:2 is for somebody; Mark 6:19 is against somebody.
cards.spotIt: Ask: does this help someone, or hurt someone?
cards.bookDef: Denotes the person (or rarely, the thing) to whose benefit or detriment a verbal action occurs.

examples.english: like a bride adorned *for her husband*
examples.note: Advantage — she is dressed for his benefit.

examples.english: So Herodias held a grudge *against him*
examples.note: Disadvantage — the grudge is to his cost.

cards.name: Possession
cards.eli5: It is theirs, said backwards. “To you is the promise” means “you have the promise.”

formula.note: = X has it.

cards.oneLine: The dative owns the subject of a to-be verb.
cards.mnemonic: PORT — O: owns it.
cards.mnemonicWhy: Greek says “to me is a book” where we say “I have a book”. Flip it round and the owner appears.
cards.spotIt: A dative sitting next to εἰμί or γίνομαι? Try flipping it into “X has”.
cards.bookDef: Unique construction in which the dative possesses the subject of an equative verb (such as εἰμι or γίνομαι).
cards.watchOut: It needs the to-be verb. Without one, you are looking at something else.

examples.note: “To you is the promise” = you have the promise.

cards.name: Reference or Respect
cards.eli5: Only true about one thing. “He died TO SIN” — dead as far as sin goes, not dead all over.

formula.note: = with reference to X.

cards.oneLine: The one respect in which the statement holds.
cards.mnemonic: PORT — R: re:, like the subject line of an email.
cards.mnemonicWhy: “Re: sin — he died.” The dative names what the sentence is about, and the claim is only true about that.
cards.spotIt: Put “with reference to” in front. Does the sentence stop being odd?
cards.bookDef: Limits the extent to which something is presented as true, qualifying a statement that would otherwise not be true.
cards.watchOut: The accusative has a respect use too (Acts 2:37, “cut with respect to the heart”). Same job, different case.

examples.english: he died *to sin* once for all
examples.note: Not dead altogether — dead with reference to sin.

cards.name: Indirect Object
cards.eli5: Who you gave it to. “Give glory to God.” God is the one getting it.

formula.note: The one who receives it.

cards.oneLine: The one to whom, or for whom, the act is done.
cards.mnemonic: PORT — T: to whom. The plain one.
cards.mnemonicWhy: The commonest dative there is, and the one English already taught you: you give it TO someone.
cards.spotIt: A giving or telling verb, a direct object, and a dative — that dative is the receiver.
cards.bookDef: Indicates the one for whom or in whose interest an act is performed.
