I baptise you with water
extraQuiz.greek: ἐγὼ … *ὕδατι* βαπτίζω ὑμᾶς (Luke 3:16)
extraQuiz.english: I baptise you with water
extraQuiz.why: Water is a tool with no will of its own. MAMA — M, not agency.

extraQuiz.prompt:
τί ποιεῖτε ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν *τοῖς σάββασιν*; (Luke 6:2)
Why are you doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?
extraQuiz.greek: τί ποιεῖτε ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν *τοῖς σάββασιν*; (Luke 6:2)
extraQuiz.english: Why are you doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?
extraQuiz.why: A point on the calendar. HIT — T.

extraQuiz.prompt:
ἀλλὰ *παρρησίᾳ* περὶ τοῦ πατρὸς ἀπαγγελῶ ὑμῖν (John 16:25)
but I will tell you plainly about the Father
extraQuiz.greek: ἀλλὰ *παρρησίᾳ* περὶ τοῦ πατρὸς ἀπαγγελῶ ὑμῖν (John 16:25)
extraQuiz.english: but I will tell you plainly about the Father
extraQuiz.why: The same word the chart files under manner at Mark 8:32. A style, not a tool. MAMA — M.

extraQuiz.prompt:
ἠκολούθει δὲ *τῷ Ἰησοῦ* Σίμων Πέτρος (John 18:15)
Simon Peter was following Jesus
extraQuiz.greek: ἠκολούθει δὲ *τῷ Ἰησοῦ* Σίμων Πέτρος (John 18:15)
extraQuiz.english: Simon Peter was following Jesus
extraQuiz.why: ἀκολουθέω is a verb of following, and the chart lists following. BEAD — D.

extraQuiz.prompt:
ὁ δὲ μαθητὴς ἐκεῖνος … *συν*εισῆλθεν *τῷ Ἰησοῦ* (John 18:15)
that disciple went in with Jesus
extraQuiz.greek: ὁ δὲ μαθητὴς ἐκεῖνος … *συν*εισῆλθεν *τῷ Ἰησοῦ* (John 18:15)
extraQuiz.english: that disciple went in with Jesus
extraQuiz.why: συν- on the verb is the giveaway: he went in alongside Jesus, not using him. MAMA — A.

extraQuiz.prompt:
ὥσπερ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ποτε ἠπειθήσατε *τῷ θεῷ* (Rom 11:30)
just as you once disobeyed God
extraQuiz.greek: ὥσπερ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ποτε ἠπειθήσατε *τῷ θεῷ* (Rom 11:30)
extraQuiz.english: just as you once disobeyed God
extraQuiz.why: ἀπειθέω is a verb of obeying — disobeying is the same list. BEAD — D.

extraQuiz.prompt:
νῦν δὲ ἠλεήθητε *τῇ τούτων ἀπειθείᾳ* (Rom 11:30)
now you have received mercy because of their disobedience
extraQuiz.greek: νῦν δὲ ἠλεήθητε *τῇ τούτων ἀπειθείᾳ* (Rom 11:30)
extraQuiz.english: now you have received mercy because of their disobedience
extraQuiz.why: Slot in “because of” and it holds. BEAD — B.

extraQuiz.prompt:
καθὼς θέλετε ἵνα ποιῶσιν *ὑμῖν* οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ποιεῖτε *αὐτοῖς* ὁμοίως (Luke 6:31)
as you want people to do to you, do the same to them
extraQuiz.greek: καθὼς θέλετε ἵνα ποιῶσιν *ὑμῖν* οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ποιεῖτε *αὐτοῖς* ὁμοίως (Luke 6:31)
extraQuiz.english: as you want people to do to you, do the same to them
extraQuiz.why: The doing lands on them: they are who it is done to. PORT — T.

extraQuiz.prompt:
*συν*εζωοποίησεν *τῷ Χριστῷ* (Eph 2:5)
he made us alive together with Christ
extraQuiz.greek: *συν*εζωοποίησεν *τῷ Χριστῷ* (Eph 2:5)
extraQuiz.english: he made us alive together with Christ
extraQuiz.why: συν- again. Alongside Christ, not by means of him. MAMA — A.

extraQuiz.prompt:
*χάριτί* ἐστε σεσῳσμένοι (Eph 2:5)
by grace you have been saved
extraQuiz.greek: *χάριτί* ἐστε σεσῳσμένοι (Eph 2:5)
extraQuiz.english: by grace you have been saved
extraQuiz.why: Grace is the instrument, not a person acting. MAMA — M.

extraQuiz.prompt: until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota will pass from the law
extraQuiz.greek: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν· ἕως ἂν *παρέλθῃ* ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ, ἰῶτα ἓν ἢ μία κεραία οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου (Matt 5:18)
extraQuiz.english: until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota will pass from the law
extraQuiz.why: Aorist active subjunctive, 3rd singular, παρέρχομαι. ἕως ἄν is one of the “until” words the chart names alongside ὅταν — indefinite temporal.

extraQuiz.prompt: not one iota, not one stroke, will pass from the law
extraQuiz.greek: ἰῶτα ἓν ἢ μία κεραία *οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ* ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται (Matt 5:18)
extraQuiz.english: not one iota, not one stroke, will pass from the law
extraQuiz.why: Aorist active subjunctive, 3rd singular, παρέρχομαι — the same form as 1a, doing a different job. οὐ μή in front makes it emphatic negation: not “probably not”, but never.

extraQuiz.prompt: Jesus said to her, “Do not cling to me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father”
extraQuiz.greek: λέγει αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς, μή μου *ἅπτου*, οὔπω γὰρ ἀναβέβηκα πρὸς τὸν πατέρα (John 20:17)
extraQuiz.english: Jesus said to her, “Do not cling to me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father”
extraQuiz.why: Present middle imperative, 2nd singular, ἅπτομαι. μή plus an imperative is the imperative's prohibition — compare number 3, where μή plus an aorist subjunctive is a different mood doing the same job in English.

extraQuiz.prompt: Do not give what is holy to dogs
extraQuiz.greek: *μὴ δῶτε* τὸ ἅγιον τοῖς κυσὶν μηδὲ βάλητε τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων (Matt 7:6)
extraQuiz.english: Do not give what is holy to dogs
extraQuiz.why: Aorist active subjunctive, 2nd plural, δίδωμι. Both of the chart's conditions are met: the command is negated (μή) and the subjunctive is aorist.

extraQuiz.prompt: nor throw your pearls before pigs
extraQuiz.greek: μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἅγιον τοῖς κυσὶν *μηδὲ βάλητε* τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων (Matt 7:6)
extraQuiz.english: nor throw your pearls before pigs
extraQuiz.why: Aorist active subjunctive, 2nd plural, βάλλω. μηδέ carries the negative on from the first clause, and the verb is aorist subjunctive again.

extraQuiz.prompt: He said to the disciples, “Let us go to Judea again”
extraQuiz.greek: λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς· *ἄγωμεν* εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν πάλιν (John 11:7)
extraQuiz.english: He said to the disciples, “Let us go to Judea again”
extraQuiz.why: Present active subjunctive, 1st plural, ἄγω. First person plural is the tell: he is going too, so it is hortatory, not an imperative.

extraQuiz.prompt: And behold, Jesus met them and said, “Greetings!”
extraQuiz.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ Ἰησοῦς ὑπήντησεν αὐταῖς λέγων, *χαίρετε* (Matt 28:9)
extraQuiz.english: And behold, Jesus met them and said, “Greetings!”
extraQuiz.why: Present active imperative, 2nd plural, χαίρω. The chart's own greeting example is the singular Χαῖρε in Matt 26:49; this is the plural of the same frozen form. Nobody is being ordered to rejoice.

extraQuiz.prompt: If anyone sees his brother sinning a sin not leading to death, he will ask and God will give him life
extraQuiz.greek: *ἐάν τις ἴδῃ* τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἁμαρτάνοντα ἁμαρτίαν μὴ πρὸς θάνατον, αἰτήσει καὶ δώσει αὐτῷ ζωήν (1 John 5:16)
extraQuiz.english: If anyone sees his brother sinning a sin not leading to death, he will ask and God will give him life
extraQuiz.why: Aorist active subjunctive, 3rd singular, ὁράω (εἶδον). ἐάν plus a subjunctive is the protasis of a third class conditional — a real maybe.

extraQuiz.prompt: One of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray”
extraQuiz.greek: εἶπέν τις τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν· κύριε, *δίδαξον* ἡμᾶς προσεύχεσθαι (Luke 11:1)
extraQuiz.english: One of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray”
extraQuiz.why: Aorist active imperative, 2nd singular, διδάσκω. The form is a command, but κύριε tells you who is being addressed — you do not order the Lord about, so it lands as a request.

extraQuiz.prompt: May the God of peace himself keep your spirit and soul and body blameless
extraQuiz.greek: αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης … ὑμῶν τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ καὶ τὸ σῶμα ἀμέμπτως … *τηρηθείη* (1 Thess 5:23)
extraQuiz.english: May the God of peace himself keep your spirit and soul and body blameless
extraQuiz.why: Aorist passive optative, 3rd singular, τηρέω. An optative closing a letter is almost always this one — a prayer or benediction. Translate with “may”.

extraQuiz.prompt: Let your word be “yes, yes” or “no, no”
extraQuiz.greek: *ἔστω* δὲ ὁ λόγος ὑμῶν ναὶ ναί, οὒ οὔ (Matt 5:37)
extraQuiz.english: Let your word be “yes, yes” or “no, no”
extraQuiz.why: Present active imperative, 3rd singular, εἰμί. English needs “let” for a third person imperative, but this is a charge about how you must speak, not a toleration — so command rather than permission.

extraQuiz.prompt: Ask, and it will be given to you
extraQuiz.greek: *αἰτεῖτε* καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν, ζητεῖτε καὶ εὑρήσετε, κρούετε καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν (Matt 7:7)
extraQuiz.english: Ask, and it will be given to you
extraQuiz.why: Present active imperative, 2nd plural, αἰτέω. Imperative + καί + future indicative is the chart's conditional pattern — “come and see” = “if you come, you will see”. Here: if you ask, it will be given. It can also be read as a plain command with a promise attached; the structure is what points to conditional.

extraQuiz.prompt: Seek, and you will find
extraQuiz.greek: αἰτεῖτε καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν, *ζητεῖτε* καὶ εὑρήσετε, κρούετε καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν (Matt 7:7)
extraQuiz.english: Seek, and you will find
extraQuiz.why: Present active imperative, 2nd plural, ζητέω. Same shape a second time, and κρούετε καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται makes it three in a row — that repetition is itself the argument for reading them as conditions.
